gloss: the year of death, as the first count in memorial numbering

definitions.gloss: the year of death, counted as the first year
definitions.explanation: The starting point of the Buddhist memorial-service counting system: the year a person dies is itself counted as the "first" year. Not a separately observed occasion — funeral rites already take place that year — but the concept explains why the service held one year later is called {一周忌|いっしゅうき} rather than {二回忌|にかいき}.

examples.japanese: {一回忌|いっかいき}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{亡|な}くなった→亡くなる：02639_nakunaru⟧⟦{年|とし}→年：00486_toshi⟧そのものを⟦{指|さ}す→指す：02056_sasu⟧。
examples.english: Ikkaiki refers to the year of death itself.

examples.japanese: {一回忌|いっかいき}という⟦{言葉|ことば}→言葉：02880_kotoba⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日常|にちじょう}→日常：01595_nichijou⟧ではほとんど⟦{使|つか}われない→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: The word ikkaiki is almost never used in everyday speech.

examples.japanese: {一回忌|いっかいき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{次|つぎ}→次：00819_tsugi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{一周忌|いっしゅうき}→一周忌：06018_isshuuki⟧、⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{次|つぎ}→次：00819_tsugi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{三回忌|さんかいき}→三回忌：06019_sankaiki⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{続|つづ}く→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧。
examples.english: After ikkaiki comes isshuuki, and after that, sankaiki.

notes:
The starting point of the Japanese Buddhist memorial-service counting system: the year of death itself counts as the "first" ({一回忌|いっかいき}), so the service held one year later is ⟦{一周忌|いっしゅうき}→一周忌：06018_isshuuki⟧ (not {二回忌|にかいき}), and the one two years later is ⟦{三回忌|さんかいき}→三回忌：06019_sankaiki⟧. {一回忌|いっかいき} itself is not observed as a separate occasion — funeral rites already take place in the year of death — so the term is used mainly to explain the counting method.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{一周忌|いっしゅうき}→一周忌：06018_isshuuki⟧: the memorial service one full year after death — the occasion people actually mark
- ⟦{三回忌|さんかいき}→三回忌：06019_sankaiki⟧: the memorial service two years after death, using the same inclusive counting
